art/batch/scenes/species/autognome-phone.png
Radiant starlight and silver nebula glow stream through damaged spaceship glazing, a clear celestial source reflected in silver-blue metal, violet glass and warm brass. Layered-depth composition: one large foreground figure, a small group in the middle distance, and the threat far behind. The camera peers through a broken workshop doorway, its battered jamb visible at one edge. Outside the hull windows, far behind everything else, a monstrous shadow glides past in the star sea. A set of beast bite wounds on one elderly adult survivor's forearm is the sole gore. The old man with this wounded forearm and his elderly adult partner share one blanket, a small warmth moment to the right.

The Autognome community: small mechanical gnome-built constructs on a spaceship workshop deck, tinkering and polishing each other, with stars outside. Recompose the workshop vertically while retaining the view through its broken doorway and the three layers of depth. An adult-looking autognome mechanic occupies the left foreground of the upper scene, large from perspective, with a weathered brass face, adult proportions, articulated ivory fingers and a polishing rag. Grief shows in its expressive mature face. A small middle-distance group of adult autognomes tends a damaged companion's mechanical shoulder and cleans battered plating at a workbench. They look natural and noble. Off to the right, an unmistakably elderly adult human couple sits together beneath a plain shared blanket; the woman supports the man's one bitten forearm, holding the wound away from faces. Keep blood only on that forearm. The outer shadow stays outside and far away; add no creature within the workshop. Only people and actions fitting these depth layers appear.

art/batch/scenes/species/aven-pc.png
Hazy desert glare creates pale gold reflected sand light and long violet shadows, a visibly hot, hazy desert atmosphere with blue-green canal reflections. Figures are strung along an implied diagonal from the lower-left corner toward the upper-right, using unequal clusters with a generous quiet gap between them. The camera is a wide establishing shot from high ground. On the far horizon a lich's green storm is gathering, ominous but distant. In one sandy patch beside the lower-left canal bank, vivid red blood is soaking into the sand; that is the only gore. A smith mends a stranger's broken blade in a small warmth moment off to the right.

The Aven community inhabits a desert city of sandstone pyramids and canals. Adult bird-headed aven have clear hawk and ibis head anatomy, mature expressive eyes, feathered heads, adult bodies, and practical scholar or messenger clothing. Seen tiny within the vast city, a few scholars gather along the lower-left ledge while winged messengers fly toward the upper-right terraces, establishing the diagonal composition. The central gap keeps the diagonal implied without filling the quiet middle with people. Broad stepped sandstone roofs, triangular pyramids and turquoise canal basins define the place. The small smith and adult stranger stand at a right-side terrace workbench, the smith repairing an actual broken blade with purposeful tools. Only the green storm appears as the lich's threat on the far horizon; do not invent a close lich or an attacking army. Keep all visible blood in the single patch soaking into sand.

One cups a bowl of stew and the other holds a torn net and rests a comforting hand against their companion's arm; this is a still, quiet encounter. Behind them a few purposeful root-built features reveal the warren, including a small covered stew pot and firefly lanterns. Omit busy extra community figures so the two-character composition remains clear. Keep the cart and priest small in the upper-right middle distance. All wounds and vivid red blood belong only to the wounded adults within this cart, including its dying adult enemy; the priest's care is gentle. The terrifying original horror rises cruelly from the farther water, with no blood on its body and no second monster.

Bright storm light: dark storm clouds tear open outside, and strong shafts of sunlight pour into the lodge through its broad windows and damaged roof, illuminating wet emerald forest and warm honey-colored timber. A dense crowd fills the left half of the frame while the other half is quiet empty space. Use a close medium shot on the crowded side. An ogre war band crosses a far ridge glimpsed through a side window, tiny and distant. One fallen adult warrior lies with arrows in the back, the sole bloody injury. Small and to one side, an adult places flowers on fallen bodies: the arrow-struck warrior and one fully covered adult form beside them; no visible injury or blood on the second body.

The Bugbear community: tall furry adult bugbears in a forest hunting lodge, stalking quietly, one lying wounded in a hammock, another carving a club. The dense left-side gathering has varied mature furry faces, adult proportions, purposeful hunting clothes and grief-stricken alert expressions; one nearby bugbear carves a wooden club, another keeps a quiet low stalking posture at the window. A wounded adult rests in the hammock with clean bandages, no exposed wound or added blood. The arrows and blood belong only to the fallen adult warrior beside the small flower-laying encounter, kept away from faces. The distant ogres remain on their far ridge beyond the lodge, never enlarged into foreground attackers. Keep the entire inhabited setting inside the lodge.

The right half is spacious quiet timber and light, not a mirrored second group. Use offset window geometry, no symmetric central corridor. The dragonfly remains natural and noble, without visible blood. Allow only these people and actions that fit the diagonal arrangement. The adult strangers share a simple piece of bread near the lower-left side group. Grass and reed silhouettes frame the close viewpoint without filling the whole image.

All visible faces and entire heads must remain inside the extreme outer quarter on either side, leaving the central half of the canvas completely free of all heads and faces. Give this quiet central surface clear visual priority.

Loose, energetic hand-drawn digital sketch illustration with confident black ink lines with some visible rough construction strokes, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions and very expressive faces, flat color fills with dry-brush and pencil texture, hard-edged cel shadows with thin red-brown accent strokes in the shading, like one finished frame of modern Western animation concept art (a single illustration, no turnaround, no model sheet, no labels). Not anime, not Studio Ghibli, not painterly realism.

Every person is an adult, including the fallen soldier, grown carrying man and his adult brother. Show grief, bodily and emotional wounds and despair within a bright, vivid, colorful elemental city approach rendered in the same flat textured fills as the figures. Dazzling reflected snow light, icy blue, turquoise city accents and natural warm fire details keep it never dark, gloomy, grey or orange-only. Blood is vivid red and confined to the torn banner around the one fallen adult soldier, with no blood splatter or extra gore elsewhere. The banner is completely blank apart from that specified blood and its tears. The brother-carrying warmth moment is tiny, distant and to one side. Only the named worgs are enemies, circling the scene's outer edge.

All textiles, hanging cloths, flags, banners, sails, awnings and blankets are plain and completely blank: no symbols, emblems, pictures, writing or decorative marks. Weapons, tools and architecture have no inscriptions.

The imp flies forward in three-quarter view while turning its head back mid-flight. Make it small and mischievous rather than monstrous: a clearly mature adult face with angular cheekbones, subtle brow wrinkles, pointed ears, a wry expression and adult proportions. Correct anatomy: exactly two arms, two legs, two bat wings attached at the upper back and one continuous tail ending in a single stinger. The wings support the flight pose and the tail curls clear of the limbs. Use a nonsexual stylized creature body with no anatomical sexual detail, and keep the complete creature within the frame.

Subject: Imp: a tiny red devil with bat wings and a stinger tail. Natural or noble creature: no blood on it except from its own wounds.

Style line: loose energetic hand-drawn sketch illustration (ink lines, flat textured color, hard shadows), bright colorful light on the creature, transparent background, natural and clean, only its own wounds if any

Create one full-body creature on a genuine transparent alpha background, 1024x1024 square. Use the exact pose and visibly colored body lighting described above. Center the whole creature, with its longest visible dimension occupying about 75 percent of the canvas; keep clear transparent margins on every side and never clip any limb, wing, ear, horn, toe, fin or tail. Three-quarter view unless the stated pose faces the viewer. Sketchy ink lines, flat textured color and hard-edged shadows; readable at 96x96 pixels with one clear silhouette. No scenery: include only things attached to the body or held by it. The entire surrounding canvas is empty and transparent, with no ground, floor, rock, perch, plants, water, backdrop, colored rectangle, painted aura, detached shadow, particles or checkerboard. Colored light belongs visibly on the creature itself. Honor the Subject’s natural or noble label; use natural anatomy and a natural expressive face. Every person is an adult.

ART STYLE: loose, energetic hand-drawn digital sketch illustration with confident black ink lines with some visible rough construction strokes, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions and very expressive faces, flat color fills with dry-brush and pencil texture, hard-edged cel shadows with thin red-brown accent strokes in the shading, like one finished frame of modern Western animation concept art (a single illustration, no turnaround, no model sheet, no labels). Not anime, not Studio Ghibli, not painterly realism.

art/batch/monsters/aberration/spectator.png
Snow-white highlights and crisp blue cel shadows illuminate a smaller floating beholder kin. It hangs angled forward with a victim's vivid-red blood dripping from the underside of its mouth, its four eyestalks spread in a wary, predatory arc.

Give the spectator a compact lopsided blue cartoon orb, a sharply angled expressive central brow, and exactly four stalks drawn as strong loose curves, each tipped with a simple flat iris and black pupil. Snow-white light is one solid graphic highlight patch, not reflected wet shine. Its one blank gold coin is a broad flat ochre disk between bold tooth wedges. The victim's blood is one flat vivid-red attached drip at the lower mouth, clearly stylized and localized.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

art/batch/monsters/aberration/mind-flayer.png
Coral light rakes across the tentacled face and sea-blue light shapes the folded dark robes. A fully adult mind flayer stands in the still aftermath of a kill, shoulders squared, with a victim's vivid-red blood dripping from its lowest facial tentacle.

Give the adult mind flayer a long angular cartoon head, a steep black-ink brow and four broad ribbon-like facial tentacles with confident curved contours; cold intent eyes are simple flat shapes. Its dark robes form two or three large angular color masses, with a few purposeful pencil fold marks. Coral and sea-blue illumination stays in flat cel bands. The one bloodied tentacle tip is a clean vivid-red graphic shape and a single attached drip, not glistening flesh.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

The small smith and adult stranger stand at a right-side terrace workbench, the smith repairing an actual broken blade with purposeful tools. Rose light illuminates the swollen brain folds and pale-green rim light picks out the long clawed legs. The intellect devourer crouches low to strike, all four legs bent like tense springs with the brain leaning eagerly forward.

Construct the intellect devourer from a few oversized flat rose brain lobes outlined with thick irregular black S-curves, a handful of drawn vein strokes and exactly four long bent clawed legs. Pale-green light forms one hard-edged shadow band, never glossy anatomical shading. The crouch uses loose visible joint arcs and emphatic cartoon angular feet. Keep it eyeless and faceless. Its single lower-fold injury is one small flat vivid-red slash, not a realistically exposed brain surface.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

art/batch/monsters/aberration/neogi.png
Snow-white light rims the spider legs and cool blue light follows the long eel neck. The neogi stalks forward one careful jointed step at a time, its neck curling down toward the viewer and its predatory mouth held half open.

Draw the adult neogi as a compact flat spider-body oval, eight clearly bent ink-defined legs and one long eel neck shaped like an expressive hooked brush gesture. Its predatory eyes and mouth are simple graphic black-and-white shapes, not realistic animal anatomy. Snow-white and blue form two or three large flat values per body part; a few coarse pencil ticks imply bristles. The abdomen scrape is one narrow vivid-red flat mark, with no modeled flesh or micro-scaled eel skin.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

art/batch/monsters/aberration/grell.png
Sky-blue light shapes the floating brain folds and clean white highlights catch the hooked beak. The grell hangs tilted toward the viewer, a victim's vivid-red blood dripping from one lowered barbed tentacle beneath its brain body.

Build the eyeless grell from a few big sky-blue brain-lobe shapes, thick black S-curve fold marks, one broad ivory hooked beak and ten freely sweeping barbed tentacle gestures. White light is a simple solid highlight patch, not photographic sheen. Keep the entire brain graphic and opaque, not anatomical translucent tissue; there are no eyes. Each barbed tentacle has a broad flat silhouette. The one bloodied lowered tentacle uses a single vivid-red graphic stain and attached drip.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

art/batch/monsters/dragon/ancient-red-dragon.png
Coral light strikes the ancient red dragon's massive head and sea-blue light shapes its folded wings. It crouches low to strike, hind legs loaded under its weight, its cruel head extended with fire curling from the jaws and blood on the teeth.

Design the crouching ancient red dragon as a forceful animation character with a huge angular snout, heavy black brows, broad folded wing triangles and a few large crimson body masses. Use coral and sea-blue as sharply bounded cel-light planes, and only occasional ink chevrons to suggest scales. Fire at the jaws is a flat red-orange flame shape, not a particle simulation. The held broken tower spire is one bold stone wedge with a few drawn cracks. Blood on the teeth is a narrow stylized vivid-red graphic accent, without wet gum rendering.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

Preserve the curling fire at its jaws, the broken spire and the complete tail and wing tips; no tower landscape or victims.

Honey-colored light warms the yellowed bones and mint light defines the spaces between the ribs. The dracolich thrusts its foretalons forward mid-attack, its skeletal dragon head lunging after them as green soulfire burns along the exposed spine.

Build the attacking dracolich as a legible ink cartoon skeleton: a broad angular skull, black open rib gaps, simple ivory rib arcs, boldly articulated vertebrae, sweeping wing spars and strong foretalon gestures. Honey and mint light are flat cel planes on the bones; bone has no bevels, pores or polished 3D shading. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

art/batch/monsters/fiend/marilith.png
Sky-blue light flows over the coiled serpent tail and white highlights catch the six blades. The marilith rears to her full height, a fully adult female demon rising above her heavy coils with all six armed hands poised in an uneven threatening fan.

Design the rearing adult marilith as a bold expressive cartoon woman demon with six clearly separated arm gestures, six broad flat blade silhouettes and a few huge sweeping serpent coils. Her mature stern face has a sharply inked brow, simple flat eyes and emphatic graphic mouth. Sky-blue and white are only two or three cel values on each skin, cloth, metal and tail surface. Scales are sparse drawn ticks, never glossy snakeskin microtexture. The single tail-coil wound is a narrow flat vivid-red shape and all six blades remain clean.

GRAPHIC 2D DRAWING DIRECTION: This is a loose ink-and-flat-color Western-animation character drawing, with thick uneven confident BLACK ink contours, strong variable brush-line weight and visible loose construction arcs. Reduce each anatomical surface to ONLY TWO OR THREE FLAT CEL VALUES: one broad base-color mass, one sharply bounded shadow and at most one simple graphic highlight. Keep the creature built from a few LARGE COLOR MASSES, never thousands of modeled surface details. Use small pencil scratches and dry-brush grain INSIDE the flat fills; texture is drawn mark-making, not rendered skin, scales, bone pores or material simulation. Push the cartoon expression and gesture while keeping the named species anatomy true. The described eyes have a simple flat iris, black pupil and ONE tiny flat white graphic accent; supernatural eye lights are simple solid dots. Do not invent eyes on eyeless anatomy. There is no corneal rendering, radial iris microdetail, eyeball veins, photographic wet shine or reflected environment. Teeth and bone are broad flat ivory shapes with heavy black borders, never beveled or shaded like 3D objects. All blood and the one specified body injury are narrow stylized flat VIVID-RED shapes at the already specified body event, with no realistic wet gore, tissue microdetail or extra splatter. No smooth shading gradients, painterly volume, realistic microtexture, glossy shader, polished monster render, lens flare, bloom, depth of field or 3D bevel. Preserve the exact Variation color pair and pose; use the drawing method above for EVERY part of the creature.

art/batch/scenes/species/fairy-pc.png
Clear light just after rain reveals wet sparkling highlights on giant leaves and mushroom caps, with a natural rainbow over the glade. Adult figures are strung along an implied diagonal from the lower-left side to the upper-right, with open space between the side clusters. The camera is a close view through tall grass and reeds. A cursed beast lies dead and rotting beside the glade. A broken blade is stuck in this same fallen beast's body, keeping all death, decay and vivid-red gore together in one place. Small to the left side, two adult strangers share bread, the warmth moment.

CRITICAL LAYOUT: a single enormous pale green leaf rises as a quiet foreground screen across the entire middle third, from the upper edge down to the lower edge. This smooth broad leaf has minimal flat texture and no busy veins, flowers, insects, figures, heads or faces. Every person, the wounded dragonfly and every important story detail is fully confined to the extreme left quarter or extreme right quarter. The diagonal of figures is implied from the lower-left group to the upper-right group across the leaf-screen gap. No fairy, dragonfly or face appears over, in front of, or behind any part of the visible middle-third leaf. Keep the leaf softly rain-washed and luminous, not a frame or overlay.

The Fairy community: tiny winged adult fairies in a giant mushroom and flower glade, tending a wounded dragonfly and gathering dew in bluebells for the hurt. Each fairy looks unmistakably adult despite tiny scale: mature adult facial structure, wrinkles or a beard where appropriate, and adult proportions, never baby-faced. At the extreme left edge, one adult attendant tends a natural dragonfly with a clean wing dressing. At the extreme right edge, other adults collect dew in bluebell cups. All attendants remain entirely inside the outer side quarters of the canvas; none occupies the middle. The unequal-height side groups imply a diagonal across a wide clear central gap. The dragonfly remains natural and noble, without visible blood. Allow only these people and actions that fit the diagonal arrangement. The cursed beast's fallen body lies at the upper-right side of the glade, original and terrifying even in death, with its rotting hide and broken blade localized to this one corpse; no other fallen body appears. The adult strangers share a simple piece of bread near the lower-left side group. Grass and reed silhouettes frame the close viewpoint without filling the whole image.

Lilac rim illumination and broad silver highlights reveal the whole towering specter, whose poised life-draining hands hang forward while fresh vivid-red blood from an unseen adult victim drips continuously down its fingertips and ragged sleeve ends. Preserve the specified dripping pose; use short connected blood threads at the hands, not a free-floating cloud of splashes. The spectral figure holds a cruelly satisfied, merciless stillness.

Design one original adult wraith lord, unnaturally tall with a skeletal suggestion inside its translucent smoky torso, a visibly tattered and bent crown, long torn robes and elongated life-draining hands. Its robe hem tapers into the attached ghostly lower body, with the entire silhouette visible. Keep the crown simple and unlettered. The gaping face is expressive and terrifying in a stylized sketch drawing. No victim, corpse or second figure is shown.

loose energetic hand-drawn sketch illustration (ink lines, flat textured color, hard shadows), bright colorful light on the creature, transparent background, terrifying, with blood and cruelty where it fits the body

loose, energetic hand-drawn digital sketch illustration with confident black ink lines with some visible rough construction strokes, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions and very expressive faces, flat color fills with dry-brush and pencil texture, hard-edged cel shadows with thin red-brown accent strokes in the shading, like one finished frame of modern Western animation concept art (a single illustration, no turnaround, no model sheet, no labels). Not anime, not Studio Ghibli, not painterly realism.

Make this unmistakably graphic 2D cartoon concept art: thick uneven BLACK ink contours, visible loose construction strokes, exaggerated expressive features and the exact named gesture. Use ONLY two or three FLAT hard-edged cel values per body material, with sparse dry-brush or pencil marks confined within the flat fills. No tiny surface microtexture, realistic wet shine, corneal reflections, gradients or modeled volume. Eyes are simple flat pupils or graphic empty sockets with at most tiny drawn glints; bone and teeth use two broad flat tones. The described body-fitting gore is stylized flat vivid red, with no extra victim, corpse or scenery. Build the wraith from bold black-edged lilac and silver robe shards and flat dark gaps: translucent spectral body parts read as simple layered flat shapes, not volumetric smoke. Its tattered crown and life-draining hands stay rough, angular and clearly drawn, with connected flat-red dripping threads at the already described fingertips and sleeve ends.

Create one full-body creature illustration on a truly transparent 1024x1024 background. The full creature occupies about 75 percent of the canvas, centered, with generous clear space and no clipped limbs or appendages. Use a three-quarter view except where the specified pose faces the viewer. No scenery: only things attached to the body or held by it. The silhouette and defining anatomy remain readable at 96x96 pixels. Every person is an adult; humanoid undead have adult proportions and mature faces. No second character, warmth group, prey or victim is present. Cruelty and despair belong to the named monster itself. Keep the light vivid and colorful on the creature, never gloomy, grey or orange-only; use vivid red for the specifically described blood.

- WOW at first glance: striking, full of character and vivid color, with clear silhouettes, confident gesture and composition.
- Specific story details, never filler decoration. Varied faces, ages, bodies and clothes. Natural anatomy and hands.
- AI slop to avoid: random ribbons, flowers or bows added for no reason; a generic glowing star or orb as the whole idea; mushy or blurry details; broken anatomy; extra fingers; warped perspective; copy-paste duplicates; meaningless ornament; plastic skin; text-like squiggles; bland stock composition.

Never include: Text, letters, numbers, runes that look like writing, logos, watermarks, signatures or artist marks, photorealism, 3D render look, lens flare, chromatic aberration, neon or fluorescent colors (vivid natural color is wanted), user-interface overlays (the UI props requested in a batch are allowed), copies of existing film characters or scenes, or of known card and book art (Magic: The Gathering, official D&D art). Clock, watch and compass faces, dice faces, book pages, scrolls, parchment, paper sheets, notes, ledgers, letters, maps, charts, signs, banners and speech bubbles stay blank: no numbers, letters or symbols on them. When the Subject names simple pictures for a sign, banner or map (a dragon shape, a pictured shop sign, an illustrated map), draw only those pictures, never letters or writing-like marks. Card faces stay blank unless the Subject names one simple picture for the card, and even then no letters or numbers.

art/batch/monsters/undead/death-knight.png
Coral key light and sea-blue reflected light strike the armor from opposite sides. The full adult death knight stalks forward deliberately with one heavy foot stepping down, the torso slightly bent into its advance and the head turned with a cruel, merciless focus. Vivid-red blood stains one torn cloth tabard near the hip, a body-fitting sign of its brutality rather than blood on every weapon or fingertip.

One original fallen adult paladin in burning black armor, transformed into a terrifying death knight. Give the armor broad worn iron plates with sharp cel highlights and visible hand-drawn edges, an opened face guard revealing a deathly adult face, and plain faceless fire escaping practical armor joints. A charred unmarked tabard and a heavy held sword suggest its fallen sacred calling without heraldic text, runes or stock official armor. Preserve the full walking body and both boots.

art/batch/monsters/undead/nightwalker.png
Turquoise edge light and pale sand-colored broad highlights make a colossal void-born adult undead readable. The creature looms after a kill, dripping with the vivid-red blood of an unseen adult victim; connected red rivulets descend from one long forearm and along the lower ribs to dripping fingertips. Keep its towering after-kill pose grimly still and cruel, with limbs clearly separated in the full-body silhouette.

An original nightwalker: a colossal, elongated humanoid undead formed from void-dark substance, with heavy hornlike cranial projections, cavernous eye hollows, an emaciated ribbed torso and impossibly long limbs. Its menace comes from stark proportions, a relentless forward tilt and negative spaces between arms and body, not from copied official art. Preserve the creature's clear anatomy and full body despite the surreal proportions. No slain victim or detached body part is shown.

art/batch/monsters/undead/bodak.png
Sunflower-yellow light rakes one side of the burnt body while teal fill exposes the other side. The adult bodak throws its head back in a terrible shriek, jaw stretched open and tense forearms lifted, with both legs planted in an unmistakable full-body roaring gesture. A single vivid-red fresh split across its charred shoulder stains that nearby burnt skin; keep the blood constrained there.

One original bodak: an adult humanoid reduced to a burnt husk, gaunt and blackened with a long distorted face and a visibly lethal death gaze from deep hollow sockets. Use strong clean cartoon-exaggerated anatomy and torn remnants of plain burned clothing. The unnatural gaze is readable through shape and pale reflected light rather than laser beams or an effects background. Make it terrifying, cruel and merciless while retaining a distinct original design.

art/batch/monsters/undead/mummy-lord.png
Meadow-green rim light and golden key light illuminate an ancient adult mummy king lunging straight at the viewer. Foreshorten the reaching wrapped arm and drive one knee forward, while keeping every limb and the entire royal silhouette inside the canvas. A vivid-red stain blooms through a torn bandage patch on the side of its ribcage, localized and readable amid the old linen.

One original adult mummy lord, an ancient desiccated king wrapped in layered worn linen with a plain aged gold crown and a narrow collar of weathered beads. Give the skull-like face a merciless snarl and the whole body a frightening forward lunge. Keep wraps connected to the body and restrict jewelry to simple meaningful royal objects, with blank surfaces and no hieroglyphs, runes, writing or meaningless ornament. This is a complete body, including the lower wrappings and feet.

The gigantic purple worm rears up to strike with its ringed maw fully open; the heavy lower body coils underneath so the entire worm and its tail fit as one readable silhouette. A small vivid-red remnant of a recent meal clings inside one recess of the cavernous mouth, making its cruelty body-specific without coating every tooth.

One original purple worm: a gigantic burrowing segmented violet worm with thick armored body rings, a muscular flared mouth filled with inward-pointing teeth and a heavy tapering tail ending in its defining sharp venomous stinger. Keep the entire tail and stinger clearly visible beside the coiled body; the stinger is one bold outlined flat shape with two or three cel values, and it adds no new blood or gore. A torn clod of earth still clings to one flank exactly as named; it is attached to the body, with no ground plane, loose dirt spray or scenery. Emphasize the immense maw and serpentine weight with confident anatomy and a terrifying merciless predatory intent. Keep its whole coiled body visible.

art/batch/scenes/screen/learn-pc.png
Late afternoon sunlight enters through a round tavern window, distinctly honey-gold on the tabletop and teal in the wall shadows. Keep the camera at eye level across the table in a wide-room establishing view. The owl and both adult learners form ONE tiny close huddle entirely within the left third, stacked in overlapping depth rather than arranged as three heads in a horizontal row: the front owl face is centered at x=12 percent and y=44 percent, the human woman leans behind the owl with her face at x=18 percent and y=36 percent, and the broad adult dwarf leans behind the woman with his face at x=24 percent and y=29 percent. All people, eyes, hands, feathers and teaching props end at or before x=29 percent. Their compact group occupies only about 25 percent of canvas width and 35 percent of height; the room's broad empty tabletop and bright calm window wall dominate the rest of the frame. The round window is upper right, leaving the middle third quiet. Small and to one side of the huddle, the dwarf slides his mug toward the woman in a friendly gesture, keeping both hands and the mug inside that same far-left group.

Learn image: a lesson picture for new players. No blood, no wounds, no bodies, no enemies, no despair. Warm, curious and welcoming. A cozy tavern corner turned into a study: the guide owl (a round tawny barn owl with a cream heart-shaped face, small round brass spectacles, a worn green canvas satchel across its chest, simple friendly eyes; the same owl that guides the app tour) stands on a stack of closed books on a wooden table, pointing a wing at one large blank twenty-sided die, while two adult adventurers (a human woman with a pencil behind her ear and a broad dwarf man with a braided beard) lean in, curious and smiling. A blank character card, a quill and a mug sit on the table.

loose energetic hand-drawn sketch illustration (ink lines, flat textured color, hard shadows, expressive cartoon faces), bright and colorful environment, warm and welcoming, no gore

loose, energetic hand-drawn digital sketch illustration with confident black ink lines with some visible rough construction strokes, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions and very expressive faces, flat color fills with dry-brush and pencil texture, hard-edged cel shadows with thin red-brown accent strokes in the shading, like one finished frame of modern Western animation concept art (a single illustration, no turnaround, no model sheet, no labels). Not anime, not Studio Ghibli, not painterly realism.
Apply this drawing treatment to every person, animal, prop and environment fragment: bold visible black ink contours, confident rough construction strokes, crisp two-dimensional silhouettes and only two or three flat cel values per material. Keep dry-brush and pencil texture sparsely inside the fills. Maintain the specified light and color as graphic flat shapes, without depth of field, photographic foreground blur, bokeh, volumetric haze, three-dimensional modeling or continuous surface gradients. Only the required rough brush transition at the outer paper or transparent edge is softly transitional. Preserve the established adult faces, adult body diversity, species traits, clothing and gestures. This Learn picture remains warm, curious and welcoming, with no gore, blood, wounds, bodies, enemies or despair.
For the tavern study, ink the owl, both adult learners, books, completely blank die and character card, quill, mug, table and round window with the same crisp two-dimensional linework. Use a few broad honey-gold and teal wall/table planes, not modeled woodgrain, stonework, tiny floorboard seams, window reflections or diffuse photographic sunlight.
Use a normal landscape canvas targeting 2400x1344, about 1.786:1, never an ultra-wide banner. Follow the original left-third composition with a physically small close huddle in depth, not a wide horizontal lineup. The owl is the frontmost member, standing on the full stack of closed books; the woman leans immediately behind and slightly above the owl, and the dwarf leans immediately behind and slightly above the woman. Their heads form a short steep diagonal rising toward the back: owl center x=12 percent/y=44 percent, woman center x=18 percent/y=36 percent, dwarf center x=24 percent/y=29 percent. Each complete head is only about five percent of canvas width, with the dwarf's far cheek, ear, hair and beard ending before x=28 percent. Preserve every adult species feature and the broad dwarf body, but overlap shoulders in depth to fit the narrow space instead of spreading the figures sideways. All story elements fit approximately inside x=4 to 29 percent and y=25 to 60 percent: only about a quarter of image width and a third of image height. Leave a clear margin before the left paper edge so the owl's whole wing, satchel, feet and book stack are visible. The owl points its wing toward the entire large blank twenty-sided die near x=20 percent/y=55 percent; the completely blank character card, quill and all other teaching props remain together in the same narrow left area. The dwarf's short friendly mug slide happens beside the woman near x=22 to 26 percent, with the mug and both adults' natural hands clearly visible within the huddle. Every head, eye, expressive hand, shoulder, sleeve, elbow, beard, feather, satchel, book, die, card, quill and mug ends at or before x=29 percent. From x=30 percent across the entire middle third and right side, show only broad empty honey-gold tabletop and a few calm teal-and-cream wall or window planes: no additional person, face, eye, hand, wing, prop or decorative focal object. Place the simple round sunlit window in the upper-right background, away from the central quiet wall. Use minimal simple outlines and a few flat color planes there, without woodgrain, fine plank seams, small window panes, masonry joints, extra chairs, plants or microdetail. Keep every required figure and teaching object safely in the middle 80 percent of height and preserve the four-edge cream-paper brush fade.

Quality bar:
- WOW at first glance: striking, full of character and vivid color, with clear silhouettes, confident gesture and composition.
- Specific story details, never filler decoration. Varied faces, ages, bodies and clothes. Natural anatomy and hands.
- AI slop to avoid: random ribbons, flowers or bows added for no reason; a generic glowing star or orb as the whole idea; mushy or blurry details; broken anatomy; extra fingers; warped perspective; copy-paste duplicates; meaningless ornament; plastic skin; text-like squiggles; bland stock composition.
Never include:
Text, letters, numbers, runes that look like writing, logos, watermarks, signatures or artist marks, photorealism, 3D render look, lens flare, chromatic aberration, neon or fluorescent colors (vivid natural color is wanted), user-interface overlays (the UI props requested in a batch are allowed), copies of existing film characters or scenes, or of known card and book art (Magic: The Gathering, official D&D art). Clock, watch and compass faces, dice faces, book pages, scrolls, parchment, paper sheets, notes, ledgers, letters, maps, charts, signs, banners and speech bubbles stay blank: no numbers, letters or symbols on them. When the Subject names simple pictures for a sign, banner or map (a dragon shape, a pictured shop sign, an illustrated map), draw only those pictures, never letters or writing-like marks. Card faces stay blank unless the Subject names one simple picture for the card, and even then no letters or numbers.
